execSummary.titleHtml:
Your chillers throw away
your hot water.
rows: A hotel runs a small utility plant 365 days a year: chillers for comfort, hot water for rooms, kitchens and laundry, pool heating, and DG sets for outages. Hot water and laundry usually burn LPG, PNG or diesel, while the chillers next to them reject heat through cooling towers. Corporate travel buyers, owners and lenders increasingly ask for carbon per room night.

Power, heat and ESG reporting are bought from different vendors on different clocks. Solar is sized without the heat load; boilers are replaced without a plan for cheaper power; ESG data is typed in once a year. Each fix leaves money and carbon on the table.

jouleWise runs the whole decarbonisation stack: green power — intrastate and ISTS solar and wind, rooftop solar, BESS and green-market purchase, each source orchestrated to fulfil the property's demand at least cost; ABT metering and data loggers on every source and load; green heat from industrial heat pumps up to 120 °C; ergOS to meter and orchestrate both every 15 minutes; esgOS to turn the same data into audit-ready disclosure.

Cheaper green power lowers the cost of every unit of heat a heat pump makes. Thermal storage lets that heat be made in the cheapest solar blocks. ergOS proves it; esgOS reports it. Savings from one layer fund the next.

Up to 25% lower power cost on DISCOM tariff and up to 65% renewable share (reported, year 1 of ergOS). Heat-recovery heat pumps then make guest hot water from chiller heat — cooling and hot water from one kWh — and batteries cut DG hours.
Four models, mix and match: Advisory, SaaS (ergOS + esgOS), Heat Advisory, and Heat as a Service, where you pay per unit of heat and invest nothing upfront.

A four-week decarbonisation baseline on one property: power bills, DG and fuel logs, and portable heat metering on hot water, laundry and the pool — ending in one business case for the property and a template for the portfolio.
execSummary.note: Reported client impact, year 1 of ergOS; C&I client outcomes. Results vary with state, tariff structure and load profile. Hotels-specific value is quantified in the baseline.

whyNow.lede: For a hotel or hospitality group, energy and carbon now show up in corporate RFPs, certifications and owner reporting. Six pressures point at the same metered data.

drivers.title: Corporate travel buyers
drivers.text: Corporate travel programmes increasingly ask for carbon and energy per occupied room night before they sign rate agreements.

drivers.title: Certifications and platforms
drivers.text: Green building ratings and sustainability badges on booking platforms all rest on metered energy and water data.

drivers.title: Energy cost
drivers.text: Hotels usually pay commercial tariffs, among the highest per unit — and run chillers, hot water and laundry every day of the year.

drivers.title: LPG, diesel and DG
drivers.text: Hot water, laundry and pools run on LPG, PNG or diesel, and DG sets cover outages. Heat pumps and batteries replace most of that fuel.

drivers.title: Owners and lenders
drivers.text: Owners, investors and lenders want asset-level energy and carbon data; green finance prices it in. Listed groups also report BRSR Core-format data.

drivers.title: Guest expectation
drivers.text: Guests notice towel cards; they notice a hotel that runs on green power more. The claim needs a meter behind it.

stack.titleHtml:
One stack.
Every layer feeds the next.
stack.lede: Most properties buy decarbonisation in pieces. We built it as a loop: low-cost green power feeds heat pumps, storage moves heat into the cheapest blocks, ergOS runs it, esgOS proves it.

items.title: Green power
items.text: Intrastate and ISTS solar and wind, rooftop solar, BESS and green-market purchase — each source orchestrated to fulfil the property's demand at least cost.

items.title: Heat pumps
items.text: Every kWh in becomes three to four kWh of useful heat. The boiler stops burning fuel for loads up to 120 °C.

items.title: Thermal storage
items.text: Heat is made when power is cheapest and greenest, and used when the process needs it.

items.title: ergOS
items.text: Meters power, steam, fuel and water every 15 minutes; forecasts, schedules and trades; runs heat pumps against price.

items.title: esgOS
items.text: Converts the same metered data to Scope 1, 2 and 3, BRSR Core-format, CBAM, CDP and customer disclosures.

stack.calloutHtml: Why the order matters. A heat pump on grid power cuts fuel cost but, at today's grid emission factor, barely cuts carbon against gas. Put the same heat pump on green power and its heat is close to zero-carbon. Power first, then heat — from one provider.

heatPump101.lede: A heat pump is a refrigerator run the other way round. It does not make heat by burning anything — it moves heat that already exists, from a cooler place to a hotter one, and uses electricity only to do the lifting.
heatPump101.copNote: COP (coefficient of performance) = useful heat ÷ electricity. A boiler can never exceed 1; a heat pump typically delivers 2 to 5.
heatPump101.liftNote: Lift = delivery temperature minus source temperature. Recovering warm waste heat first and delivering no hotter than the process needs keeps the COP high.
faq: For loads up to 120 °C, yes — as the primary heat source. The boiler usually stays on standby and for any loads above that range.
Each kWh of power returns three to four kWh of heat, so heat costs roughly a third of the power price. On green open access, the carbon falls close to zero as well.
Spare electrical capacity, space near the heat users and a steady heat demand. A hot-water store smooths peaks and lets the unit run in the cheapest blocks.
It is the same refrigeration cycle as the chillers already on your site, run for heat. Industrial units are in service worldwide in food, chemicals, pharma and textiles.

heat.lede: Almost all hotel heat is low-temperature: showers, dishwashing, laundry and the pool sit between 26 and 82 °C. Heat pumps are built for this — and the chillers already on site supply the heat.

loads.name: Cooking
loads.sub: remains on PNG, LPG or induction

cards.title: Heat sources we reuse
cards.text: Chiller condensers, kitchen and laundry exhaust, and warm grey water — a hotel rejects nearly as much heat as it buys.

cards.title: Heating and cooling at once
cards.text: Hotels cool all year while making hot water all day. A heat pump on the chiller circuit delivers both, so the cooling you already pay for produces your hot water.

cards.title: Sized from metered heat
cards.text: Portable heat meters log flow and temperature on candidate processes for two to four weeks before anything is sized.

economics.lede: What one kWh of useful process heat costs, and what it emits, depending on where the heat comes from. The heat pump cuts cost on any power; green power is what cuts the carbon.

economics.note: Illustrative only, not an offer. Assumptions: PNG 10.4 kWh/SCM, 1.95 kg CO₂/SCM; HSD 10.0 kWh/L, 2.68 kg CO₂/L; grid 0.716 kg CO₂/kWh (CEA baseline order of magnitude); green power treated as zero-emission on a market basis with green attributes retired. Heat pump COP 3.5 reflects hot water near 60 °C for guest rooms, drawn from the chiller condenser loop; COP falls as delivery temperature rises. Tariffs, fuel prices and COP vary by site and are replaced with metered values in the baseline. LPG: ₹95/kg, 12.8 kWh/kg, 2.98 kg CO₂/kg. Hotels on commercial tariffs may pay more than ₹8.5/kWh from the DISCOM, which strengthens the case for green open access.
